original_value: Coverage is a vital indicator which reflects the performance of directional sensor networks (DSNs). The random deployment of directional sensor nodes will lead to many covergae blind areas and overlapping areas. Besides, the premature death of nodes will also directly affect the service quality of network due to limited energy. To address these problems, this paper proposes a new area coverage and energy consumption optimization approach based on improved adaptive particle swarm optimization (IAPSO). For area coverage problem, we set up a multi-objective optimization model in order to improve coverage ratio and reduce redundancy ratio by sensing direction rotation. For energy consumption optimization, we make energy consumption evenly distribute on each sensor node by clustering network. We set up a cluster head selection optimization model which considers the total residual energy ratio and energy consumption balance degree of cluster head candidates. We also propose a cluster formation algorithm in which member nodes choose their cluster heads by weight function. We next utilize an IAPSO to solve two optimization models to achieve high coverage ratio, low redundancy ratio and energy consumption balance. Extensive simulation results demonstrate the our proposed approach performs better than other ones.

result.paraphrase: Coverage is an important metric for assessing directional sensor networks (DSNs). Randomly deployed directional sensor nodes can create many coverage blind spots and overlapping regions. In addition, because of limited energy, early node failures directly degrade network service quality. To solve these issues, this paper presents a new area coverage and energy consumption optimization method based on improved adaptive particle swarm optimization (IAPSO). For the area coverage problem, we build a multi-objective optimization model that improves the coverage ratio and lowers the redundancy ratio by rotating sensing directions. For energy optimization, we distribute energy consumption more evenly across sensor nodes by clustering the network. We formulate a cluster-head selection optimization model that takes into account the total residual energy ratio and the energy consumption balance degree of cluster-head candidates. We also design a cluster formation algorithm in which member nodes select their cluster heads through a weight function. We then use IAPSO to solve the two optimization models and obtain high coverage ratio, low redundancy ratio, and balanced energy consumption. Extensive simulation results show that the proposed approach outperforms the others.
